Pubity on Instagram: "NASA’s Artemis II mission marks humanity’s return toward the Moon, sending four astronauts on the first crewed lunar flyby since 1972, launching from Kennedy Space Center after overcoming earlier delays. 

With about an 80% chance of favorable weather, the crew will travel around the Moon, capturing views of regions never seen directly by humans, before returning to Earth with a planned splashdown in the Pacific on April 10 after a high-speed reentry.

-
#news #viral #pubity"
content.text: Not saying it didn’t happen… but how on earth (or on the Moon) is going near or around the Moon the extent of our capabilities 57 years after we allegedly put boots on the ground?People argue it takes time to “get back into” lunar missions before landing again - but what exactly is there to get back into? This isn’t someone retraining for a marathon. It’s (allegedly) a feat accomplished nearly 60 years ago with what was, by today’s standards, extremely minimal technology manned with an entirely different crew..The Apollo 11 Guidance Computer - essentially the brain of the spacecraft - reportedly operated with just 72 KB of ROM and 4 KB of RAM. That’s roughly the equivalent of 0.03-0.06 seconds of iPhone 4 video.We supposedly reached the Moon using a computer that could barely hold a fraction of a second of phone footage - in a time before calculators were common, before email, cell phones, microprocessors, or digital photography. Yet today, with AI, advanced robotics, biotech, and quantum computing, sending humans around the Moon is treated as a massive, difficult achievement.It’s fair to wonder why something accomplished over 50 years ago now seems so hard - especially considering the last half-century has produced arguably the greatest technological leap in human history.I guess this could easily be settled by just watching the original Apollo 11 NASA footage……oh wait. Some intern allegedly taped over it.
